**Finding submitted: deviation (medium severity), Section 13 (p0047).**

**What the clause does:** Section 13 is a mutual non-solicit that binds Clear Capital as well as RadialSpark. Checking it against the fallback position:

| Fallback element | Status |
|---|---|
| Mutual | ✅ "Neither party shall..." |
| Limited to personnel involved in the services | ✅ "personnel who have had direct involvement with the Services" |
| 12 months | ✅ one (1) year — far inside the 24-month walk-away line |
| No "no-hire" | ✅ restricts "solicit for hire," not hiring itself |
| General-advertising / unsolicited-approach carve-out | ❌ **absent** |

**Why this is a deviation rather than a note:** the missing carve-out is not a stylistic gap — the rule summary makes it a condition of acceptability ("only narrow, time-limited non-solicits with a general-advertising carve-out"). As drafted, Clear Capital could technically breach by running an untargeted job posting that a RadialSpark engineer happens to answer, or by hiring someone who approaches us unprompted. The "consent not unreasonably withheld" proviso softens this but does not cure it.

**Remedy chosen:** the smallest edit that reaches the fallback — one appended sentence carving out (a) untargeted general solicitations and (b) responses to them or unsolicited approaches. I deliberately did **not** push for the preferred position (no non-solicit on Customer), since the clause is genuinely mutual and already narrow in scope and duration; demanding its deletion would be disproportionate to the existing bargain.

**Noted in the rationale, not flagged:** the one-year period runs from termination of the Agreement rather than from the end of the individual's involvement with the Services. This is marginally broader than the preferred formulation but remains well within the 24-month tolerance, so it is a minor sub-element rather than an independent breach.
